claims.reasoning: No quoted passage establishes the claimed absence; the passages contain no explicit statement about processing air before the lungs, so the meta-claim remains unsupported rather than contradicted.

claims.claim_text: The trend towards self-diagnosis through lab testing, with a view to preempting disease, is growing in the US.
claims.reasoning: The cited premises together entail a growing US trend of individuals obtaining lab tests themselves for screening/preventive purposes; there is no contradiction.

citations.quote: A frothy private sector is gearing up to serve the "test me" market.  In those states that allow it -- and over half do -- laboratories are offering walk-in and online services to individuals who want to check their own lab values.
Following her mother's cancer diagnosis, singer Taylor Swift urged her fans to remind their parents to get screening tests.
And Arizona Gov. Doug Ducey signed legislation to allow Arizonans to get any lab test without a doctor's order.
The biotech sector is excited about testing well people -- it's a huge market -- and is developing lots of new product.

claims.claim_text: Over half of states allow walk-in and online lab services without a doctor's order.
claims.reasoning: The source directly says over half of states allow this and that the offered walk-in/online services correspond to testing without a doctor's order (Arizona example).

citations.quote: In those states that allow it -- and over half do -- laboratories are offering walk-in and online services to individuals who want to check their own lab values.
And Arizona Gov. Doug Ducey signed legislation to allow Arizonans to get any lab test without a doctor's order.

claims.claim_text: Critics of the trend argue that it is likely to lead to more medical care rather than improved health.
claims.reasoning: The passage explicitly says the primary effect will be more medical care rather than more health, matching the claim's content.

citations.quote: Some might argue that this freedom to test is the path to a healthier society. But the primary effect won't be more health, but rather more medical care.

claims.claim_text: Patients present themselves to doctors with abnormal results that are often false positives or minor abnormalities.
claims.reasoning: Both the abnormal results presentation and their frequent false-positive/minor nature are directly stated.

citations.quote: Fundamentally well people will appear in doctors' offices with "abnormal" results.
Further testing will often make clear that the initial results were false alarms.  Or it will confirm the presence of abnormality -- most of which will be minor abnormalities.

claims.claim_text: Further testing can lead to increased anxiety, more procedures and over-treatment for diseases unlikely to cause problems.
claims.reasoning: The three elements of the claim are directly enumerated as side-effects of testing.

citations.quote: Decades of research have shown that there are real side-effects to testing the well: more anxiety (that can't be good for your health), more procedures (which often involve needles, pain and can even lead to complications like collapsed lungs) and more treatment for "disease" not destined to cause problems

claims.claim_text: The trend is likely to increase healthcare costs through the sheer volume of additional testing and subsequent office visits for abnormal results.
claims.reasoning: The cost-increase mechanism (volume of testing plus office visits and follow-up for abnormal results) is directly described.

citations.quote: Sure, a competitive market will drive down prices for individual tests.   But advertising will drive up the volume of testing.  And then there are all the office visits and subsequent testing for the abnormal results.  This will cost people real money -- either in terms of higher insurance premiums or higher out-of-pocket costs.

claims.claim_text: Diagnostic tests can be extremely useful in sorting out acute medical problems.
claims.reasoning: The passage explicitly states that diagnostic tests can be extremely useful in sorting out acute medical problems.

citations.quote: Diagnostic tests can be extremely useful in sorting out acute medical problems.

claims.claim_text: Diagnostic tests are not necessarily useful for routine check-ups.
claims.reasoning: The cited text directly denies routine usefulness and distinguishes acute use from testing well people, matching the claim's qualified scope.

citations.quote: Diagnostic tests can be extremely useful in sorting out acute medical problems.
But if you feel well, don't think that testing will make you feel better.
The public needs to know that while medical data can be very useful, that doesn't mean they are routinely useful.

claims.claim_text: Critics argue that the sector is in need of regulation and public education about what test results indicate and how to respond to them.
claims.reasoning: The passage states the author's own view that testing demands regulation and education, but the claim's attribution to critics is not supported by any quoted premise.

citations.quote: Considering the Academy of Country Music Awards celebrated its 50th anniversary on Sunday night at the Dallas Cowboys stadium, it was bound to be bigger than any previous year's ACMs.

The Best. Eric Church & Keith Urban provide an opening wallop. With a full stadium and millions of home viewers watching, two of country's leading men successfully lit the fuse for the 50th annual ACM Awards with a slick joint kickoff performance. Eric Church's "Pledge Allegiance To The Hag" was a fine throwback, but Keith Urban's powerhouse "Raise 'Em Up" lived up to its title -- and then some. Setting a Guinness World Record. Not only was this the ACMs biggest audience ever, but the 2015 ACM Awards brought in the biggest audience for a live TV awards show ever. Now that's how you celebrate half a century. Reba McEntire demonstrates how it's done. During a night that found a couple performers sounding a little weak in the vocal department, Reba McEntire showed the entire Cowboys stadium -- and many younger singers who don't have half her energy -- how it's done. Reba is eternal. Taylor Swift singing in the audience. Whether it was during Eric Church or Martina McBride, T-Swift was heating up the audience by singing and swaying along to country staples. Taylor might have gone pop for "1989," but she was deep in the heart of Texas for this annual country extravaganza.
